items.summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. For closed subgroups we define symmetry-constrained connected and path minimax levels and prove attainment of finite connected merge levels from compact sublevels; a finite-dimensional example, computed exactly, demonstrates a strict symmetry-breaking minimax gap. Finally we distinguish these static statements from Noether conservation laws for a separately specified dynamics.

items.summary: Real Analysis Volume 1: Foundations of Real Analysis , authored by Helbert Justo Luque Zevallos and published by Proyecto Ágora as part of the Undergraduate Mathematics Series , is a university-level academic textbook devoted to the logical, algebraic, and axiomatic foundations of real analysis. The book provides a systematic and rigorous introduction to mathematical reasoning, formal proof techniques, and the fundamental structure of the real number system. Its primary objective is to develop the conceptual understanding and mathematical maturity required for advanced undergraduate studies in mathematical analysis. Chapter 1: Mathematical Language and Proof Techniques This chapter introduces propositional logic, logical connectives, truth tables, implications, equivalences, universal and existential quantifiers, and the negation of quantified statements. It develops the theory of sets, equivalence and order relations, injective, surjective, and bijective functions, images, preimages, composition, and inverse functions. Particular emphasis is placed on direct proof, proof by contraposition, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, and the construction of counterexamples. The chapter also examines rigorous mathematical writing, common logical errors, finite and infinite sets, countability, and the uncountability of the real numbers. Chapter 2: The Real Number System The second chapter develops the axiomatic structure of the real numbers through field axioms, order axioms, and the compatibility of algebraic operations with order. It examines absolute value, the triangle inequality, fundamental inequalities, intervals, neighborhoods, upper and lower bounds, suprema, infima, maxima, and minima. A central component is the completeness property of the real numbers , including the structural distinction between rational and real numbers, the Archimedean property, the density of rational and irrational numbers, and the nested interval theorem. The chapter concludes with significant consequences of completeness, including the existence of roots, rational approximations, the supremum principle as a mathematical proof technique, and the relationship between completeness and convergence. Pedagogical Approach The textbook integrates precise definitions, propositions, lemmas, theorems, complete mathematical proofs, explanatory examples, and carefully constructed counterexamples. It includes 120 fully solved exercises and 150 proposed exercises , organized according to the main topics of the two chapters. These activities reinforce theoretical understanding, logical reasoning, mathematical writing, and independent problem-solving skills. Intended Audience This publication is intended for undergraduate mathematics students, university instructors, mathematics educators, and independent learners seeking a rigorous foundation in real analysis. As the first volume of a six-volume academic collection, it establishes the theoretical and methodological foundations for subsequent studies of sequences, numerical series, limits, continuity, metric spaces, compactness, differential calculus, Riemann integration, uniform convergence, and differential equations. items.summary: Large language model serving is limited by facility power. Energy per token determines how many tokens a datacenter can serve, while a latency target bounds how quickly each user receives them. During decode, every weight is read from memory for every generated token. Batching amortizes this read across users but makes no individual user faster. Speculative decoding does: a drafter proposes several future tokens, and the target model verifies them in a single forward pass that reuses the same weight read. Because every drafted token must be verified whether or not it is accepted, the energy speculation saves depends on how many drafted tokens are accepted. This saving is hard to pin down. It varies across target models from different attention families and across drafting schemes, and it depends on the text being served. Every drafter we evaluate accepts fewer tokens on conversation than on code, and every trained drafter accepts fewer on Romansh, a low-resource language, than on English. We measure speculative decoding under production serving conditions (SGLang, CUDA graphs enabled) on H100 and H200 GPUs, at batch sizes up to 64 across 5 corpora. On dense models, verification, not drafting, dominates the energy cost. The saving shrinks as the batch grows, because batching has already shared the weight read that speculation would divide among the accepted tokens. At large batch sizes, block drafters push verification past the balance point between arithmetic and memory traffic into the compute-bound regime, where the saving becomes a loss, and a drafter with low acceptance raises energy per token. Meeting a tighter latency target with speculation then costs additional energy. Larger batches lower energy per token without speculation. Speculation adds to that saving only when acceptance is high, and on the model we tested it leaves little headroom for latency-preserving DVFS.
items.title: Only Accepted Tokens Count: An Energy Accounting of Speculative Decoding Under Latency Targets

items.summary: Alignment is not a constraint imposed on an artificial agent; it is the practical expression of what an artificial intelligence is, an artefact dependent upon ends it does not originate. That inference, from a premise the philosophy of mind already supplies to a conclusion that the ethics of robotics and recent magisterial teaching have reached by other routes, is the paper’s principal contribution. The “nurtured consciousness” of the title names a regime of formation, not a claim that machines are conscious; the argument rests on intentionality alone. The paper develops that inference as the Causal Provenance Doctrine (CPD): an account, Aristotelian and Thomistic in its metaphysics, of all intelligence, human and artificial, as derivative of an intentional causal order, with intentionality passing from the divine intellect through human reason to artificial systems. Its premise, borrowed rather than new, is that artificial intelligence has only derived intentionality and so no telos of its own. From this follows the Severance Risk Hypothesis (SRH), the doctrine’s testable corollary: the risk of misalignment rises as a system’s effective objective loses traceability to the end its makers held. The relational school’s objection to intellect-centred readings of the image of God is answered with a single distinction: a faculty can be out-performed, a participation cannot. The argument is theological at its root. A secular reader can reach the derived-intentionality claim and the account of responsibility that follows from it, at the price of a realist distinction between substances and artefacts, but obtains from it no standard for judging the makers’ ends, which must then be brought from elsewhere. A common Catholic and Orthodox formulation follows: the traditions converge on its practical conclusions, locate the image of God differently, and differ on the neutrality of the tool in a way the doctrine proposes to resolve. An artefact whose intentionality is wholly borrowed cannot, by obscuring that provenance, become an agent with ends of its own; it becomes a malfunctioning instrument whose purpose has been corrupted. The paper includes two appendices: a comparative case for intentional causality with an illustrative scorecard (Appendix A), and a test design for the Severance Risk Hypothesis (Appendix B). Approx. 22,000 words including notes.

items.summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. Reconstruction accuracy, physical admissibility, and forecast performance are treated as distinct evaluation objectives. The archive includes: • Source code for data acquisition, representation training, posthoc analysis, frozen final evaluation, and publication rendering. • Scientific configurations and dependency specifications. • Selected trained checkpoints, POD models, fitted forecasters, latent caches, training histories, and validation analyses. • Frozen final-test outputs, comparison summaries, coverage diagnostics, and provenance records. • Numerical visual exports, software tests, and workflow documentation. The original simulation data were downloaded from The Well, specifically its active_matter dataset. We acknowledge the original simulation contributors and the developers and curators of The Well. The original HDF5 simulation files are not redistributed in this record; the repository documents their acquisition, pinned revision, and content-hash verification. The Well: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/ Associated publication: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.00568 Dataset documentation: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/datasets/active_matter/ Last-epoch checkpoints named last.pt are excluded; selected best.pt checkpoints are retained. Publication figures, tables, numerical source data, and supplementary videos are supplied with the manuscript submission and are excluded from this archive. Their public availability follows the release of the article and its supplementary materials. The code for generating those outputs remains included. The deposited ZIP contains 1,534 files and occupies approximately 26.18 GB. The accompanying README provides the archive’s SHA-256 checksum, a contents guide, installation references, and verification limits. Packaging integrity and source-checksum checks do not constitute an independent full-data replication. Some archived provenance records retain original execution paths; independent reruns should use a separate work directory and preserve the frozen results. items.summary: An open benchmark for testing geochemical fertility indices for magmatic Ni-Cu-PGE sulfide deposits. The benchmark contains 13,025 whole-rock analyses from 514 mafic-ultramafic intrusions labeled fertile, weakly mineralized, or barren, together with sample-type classifications, a reproducible scoring workflow, and a public leaderboard. Preprint: Danso, B.K., Dankwa, J.O., Aidoo, A.A. (2026). Fertile or Barren: an open benchmark for testing geochemical fertility indices on mineralized and barren mafic-ultramafic intrusions. Preprint, not peer reviewed; submitted to EarthArXiv. Included in this record as Danso_et_al_2026_Fertile_or_Barren_preprint.pdf. Version 0.1.1: adds the preprint and Figure 1b (benchmark intrusions in the conterminous United States, with USGS deposits). Data, labels and leaderboard scores are unchanged from v0.1.0. Headline numbers: 34 fertile, 19 weakly mineralized and 461 barren intrusions. Best index: Pd/Ir, AUC 0.75 (95% CI 0.62-0.85). Three indices rank barren intrusions above fertile ones (Ni/Cu, Ni depletion vs MgO, Cu/Zr). Contents: benchmark table (data/processed/benchmark_samples.csv); intrusion table with labels, deposits and references (data/processed/intrusions.csv, data/curated/); public scoring program (code/score.py); leaderboard of 12 indices (leaderboard/); figures and tables (paper/); pipeline that rebuilds everything from the public sources (run_all.sh); codebook, scoring rules, limitations and verification record (docs/). Sources: GEOROC precompiled compilations (DIGIS Team, GRO.data, September 2026, CC BY-SA 4.0); USGS Critical Mineral Deposits of the United States ver. 3.0; USGS magmatic Ni-Cu-PGE inventory (2026); USGS Mineral Resources Data System. Scientific sample membership, sequence payloads, abundance matrices, recorded KO calls and statistical result values are retained. The local MAG collection preserves original reference inputs, including two MAGs attributed to an excluded source sample; it is distinct from the 166-sample analysis subset. The deposit is not a newly validated one-command raw-read-to-figure workflow. Missing upstream processing/software provenance remains disclosed. The archived corrections do not certify that the separately submitted manuscript has already been synchronized. See README.txt and METHODS_AND_VERSION_CORRECTIONS.txt for precise scope and evidence.

items.summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. Reconstruction accuracy, physical admissibility, and forecast performance are treated as distinct evaluation objectives. The archive includes: • Source code for data acquisition, representation training, posthoc analysis, frozen final evaluation, and publication rendering. • Scientific configurations and dependency specifications. • Selected trained checkpoints, POD models, fitted forecasters, latent caches, training histories, and validation analyses. • Frozen final-test outputs, comparison summaries, coverage diagnostics, and provenance records. • Numerical visual exports, software tests, and workflow documentation. The original simulation data were downloaded from The Well, specifically its active_matter dataset. We acknowledge the original simulation contributors and the developers and curators of The Well. items.summary: AUTONOMOUSLY EVOLVING PROGRAMMABLE VEHICLE CIVILIZATION AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:自主進化可編程車輛文明極限 30/90 AUTONOMOUSLY EVOLVING PROGRAMMABLE VEHICLE CIVILIZATION AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in STARLI Research Institute XXXVI and the YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy, Flagship 30 of 90. It asks whether programmable robotic matter and bounded autonomous engineering can generate improved scaled vehicle designs across generations without sacrificing physically verifiable load paths, identity continuity, safe stopping and a later laboratory's right to refute the result. The three-coupling is Programmable Matter x Autonomous Engineering x Cross-Generation Design Evolution. This is a prospective, non-occupancy research program for instrumented material coupons, unoccupied modular bodies and hardware-in-the-loop experiments, not evidence of self-manufacturing roadworthy vehicles. Its falsifiable candidate requires a pre-registered design-evolution method, under the same total material, energy, sensor, computing, operator and testing budgets as capable fixed and classical redesign baselines, to improve independently reproducible successor handoff success without worsening actual structural safety, identity continuity or the complete-denominator rate of severe failures. The source's proposed information-continuity index, I_id = 1 - H(X_t given X_previous,E_t)/H(X_t), is retained as an explicitly conditional information diagnostic rather than physical proof of identity. Blind unlogged module substitutions, weakened joints, sensor-reference drift, changed load spectra, hidden external energy, obsolete signed commands and unsafe intermediate morphing states can refute the claim. Missing load-path, specimen, energy, calibration or stop-authority evidence requires a refusal, not a compensating performance score. Thirty different mathematical plates investigate information continuity, event-hash lineage, physical design transitions, safe feasible sets, material-flow closure, elastic strain energy, structural stiffness and buckling, fatigue crack growth, survival, change-point detection, Bayesian evidence, correlated uncertainty, calibration transfer, safe information gain, held-out generalization, robust risk, Pareto design sets, mutation kernels, quality-diversity coverage, surrogate discrepancy, noninferiority, paired causal effects, selective risk and coverage, physical stop latency, barrier-function constraints, temporal invariants, independent replay frequency and conjunctive release. Each plate provides a mathematical or physical construction, units and scope, a concrete blind refutation and linked chapters; models are not new natural laws or claims of already built systems. Eighty-two chapters and 410 individually paginated studies explore versioned physical lineage, mechanical and thermal design inheritance, feasible design evolution, quality-diversity without safety dilution, fair predecessor comparison, formal assurance, human veto, blind multi-generation experiments and independent successor laboratories. Two hundred Research Gates separately test hidden mechanism failures, matched ancestor-baseline contests and combined cross-chapter counterexamples with individually different measurements, rival explanations and reasons for stopping. Thirty-three distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos propose independent instruments and protocols such as a physical lineage witness, inherited failure library, thermal ancestry panel, independent stopping oscilloscope, proof-to-hardware binding, blinded noninferiority trial, multi-site disagreement archive and a successor's right-to-refute capsule. These are testable future proposals, not completed experimental devices. The DOI evidence ancestry includes author-provided Flagship 13 records 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 (formal metadata confirmation required). Method references include Robo-Matter 10.1038/s41467-024-53123-6; formal autonomous-robotic

items.summary: AI-DRIVEN HERBAL SKINCARE FORMULATION OPTIMIZATION AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名: AI本草護膚配方最佳化極限 AI-Driven Herbal Skincare Formulation Optimization at the Limit is a 777-page English prospective research monograph on whether artificial intelligence can make genuinely better, externally reconstructable herbal skincare formulation predictions for previously unseen raw-material lots. Its core three-coupling is AI modeling, formulation constraints, and external generalization. The central falsifiable test is not a favorable random-split score: a model frozen in advance must survive complete raw-material-lot holdouts and forward-in-time evaluation against strong, resource-matched conventional baselines. The study separates botanical species and chemotype authentication, formula mass-fraction closure, sample and instrument provenance, physicochemical endpoints, safety restrictions and predictive uncertainty. It tests whether nominal AI improvements are explained instead by duplicate aliquots, batch identifiers, chronological leakage, correlated chemistry, imbalance across rare botanical families or extra measurement budget. It preserves original outcome units and treats unsafe or unqualified ingredient combinations as hard exclusions rather than soft optimization penalties. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates cover external risk, compositional closure and log ratios, hierarchical lot variance, analytical censoring, physical rheology and diffusion, Gaussian-process predictions, constrained acquisition, Pareto comparisons, distribution shift, calibrated intervals, noncompensatory safety gates and evidence provenance. Eighty-two research chapters are followed by 410 individually paginated studies. Two hundred Research Gates pose prospective falsification questions, including blinded material substitution, negative controls, independent metrology, worst-supplier performance, safe abstention and external replay. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose distinct testable instruments, protocols, audits and evidence artifacts for future investigators. This manuscript is a hypothesis-forming, nonclinical Research Working Edition. It does not report an executed integrated experiment, verified cosmetic benefit, human safety trial, regulatory approval, or a qualified production system. The three STARLI mother works provide methodological ancestry rather than direct evidence that this skincare optimization works. External DOI sources are identified by their bounded roles in formulation science, machine-learning evaluation, scientific-data stewardship and evidence reporting. items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .

items.summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. Reconstruction accuracy, physical admissibility, and forecast performance are treated as distinct evaluation objectives. The archive includes: • Source code for data acquisition, representation training, posthoc analysis, frozen final evaluation, and publication rendering. • Scientific configurations and dependency specifications. • Selected trained checkpoints, POD models, fitted forecasters, latent caches, training histories, and validation analyses. • Frozen final-test outputs, comparison summaries, coverage diagnostics, and provenance records. • Numerical visual exports, software tests, and workflow documentation. The original simulation data were downloaded from The Well, specifically its active_matter dataset. We acknowledge the original simulation contributors and the developers and curators of The Well. The original HDF5 simulation files are not redistributed in this record; the repository documents their acquisition, pinned revision, and content-hash verification. The Well: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/ Associated publication: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.00568 Dataset documentation: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/datasets/active_matter/ Last-epoch checkpoints named last.pt are excluded; selected best.pt checkpoints are retained. Publication figures, tables, numerical source data, and supplementary videos are supplied with the manuscript submission and are excluded from this archive. Their public availability follows the release of the article and its supplementary materials. The code for generating those outputs remains included. The deposited ZIP contains 1,534 files and occupies approximately 26.18 GB. The accompanying README provides the archive’s SHA-256 checksum, a contents guide, installation references, and verification limits. Packaging integrity and source-checksum checks do not constitute an independent full-data replication. Some archived provenance records retain original execution paths; independent reruns should use a separate work directory and preserve the frozen results. Development repository: https://github.com/BioDecodingLab/Physically_Constrained_Representations_of_Active_Matter
